title: Bidirectional A* on LA: Real-Map Routing ⚡
description: Watch how Bidirectional A* finds a fast path on real streets by searching forward from the start and backward from the goal at the same time. It’s the core idea behind how routing AI can compute efficient routes in milliseconds under real constraints.
ig_caption:
Bidirectional A* on Real Maps: The Ultimate Pathfinding Algorithm — How autonomous vehicles and routing AI calculate optimal routes in milliseconds ⚡

In this visualization, we run Bidirectional A*: one A* wave expands from your origin, while another expands from the destination. When the two search frontiers meet, we stitch the optimal route together—often shrinking the explored area compared to one-directional search.

Key mechanics (why it’s fast):
• Two heuristics, two frontiers: forward from start, backward from goal
• Meeting condition: terminate when paths can’t improve beyond the best connecting cost
• Same graph, smarter search: fewer nodes expanded = quicker reroutes

Takeaway: bidirectional search + A* heuristics is how you keep planning responsive when the map is large and time is tight.

Debate question: Would you rather optimize for fewer expanded nodes (speed) or for guaranteed behavior across weird heuristics (stability)?
